subject.title: Bug: Control UI CSP blocks Zod Function() constructor — 'eval' violation + 401 config fetch

question: Should the Control UI standardize on early Zod jitless initialization while preserving strict `script-src`, rather than permitting full `unsafe-eval`?
rationale: The dependency directly supports the safer no-JIT path, but its import-order requirement is security-critical and the alternative intentionally broadens executable browser behavior.

options.title: Adopt early jitless initialization
options.body: Configure Zod before application imports can access its eval probe and require strict-CSP browser proof before shipping.

options.title: Replace browser-side Zod
options.body: Remove the limited browser Zod dependency if maintainers consider the import-order invariant too fragile.

options.title: Permit unsafe-eval
options.body: Relax the Control UI CSP and explicitly accept eval-equivalent execution for all same-origin scripts.

recommendation.title: Adopt early jitless initialization
recommendation.body: Configure Zod before application imports can access its eval probe and require strict-CSP browser proof before shipping.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the current assignee and introduced the central CSP/bootstrap security boundary.
